settlementFee.note: CENTRAL STRUCTURAL FINDING: unlike NY (TIRSA, premium only) and unlike PA's attorney-procedure carve-out, NEW JERSEY'S RATING BUREAU DIRECTLY REGULATES THE SETTLEMENT/CLOSING FEE ITSELF, not just the title insurance premium. NJLTIRB's Manual Article 6 ('Settlement Charges') sets a promulgated flat settlement fee: $300.00 for a settlement WITH disbursements (in-office, business hours, <=60 min), or $150.00 for a settlement WITHOUT disbursements (same conditions) -- these are the SAME uniform figures every NJLTIRB member Insurer/Title Insurance Agent is legally required to charge, confirmed independently republished byte-for-byte by two of this survey's own provider sources (World Wide Land Transfer's NJ page and Federated National Land LLC's fee schedule, both stating $300/$150). Surcharges are also promulgated: +$25 if outside the office (total $325/$175), +$50 if outside 9am-5pm business hours (total $350/$200), +$100/hour (with disbursements) or +$50/hour (without) for settlements exceeding 60 minutes. HOWEVER, several closing-adjacent service categories are explicitly left UNREGULATED and cost-based/market-set under Section 7.6: wire transfer fees, statutory notary fees, Transaction Management Platform fees, and lender/third-party closing-compliance fees -- 'the Insurer or Title Insurance Agent may charge the cost for such services' rather than a Manual-fixed number. This is the exact unregulated territory the task brief targeted, and this survey found real provider-to-provider variation there (e.g., wire fee $15 vs $25 across two verified NJ providers -- see provider entries below), even though the headline settlement fee itself is fixed by law.
settlementFee.standardUnderwritingPremiumRate_represen: Article 4.2, Standard Underwriting Rate (owner's/leasehold/mortgage insurance): $0-$100,000 = $5.25/thousand; add $4.25/thousand from $100,001-$500,000; add $2.75/thousand from $500,001-$2,000,000; add $2.00/thousand over $2,000,000. Minimum Underwriting Charge in any transaction: $200.00 (Section 4.1). Example: $200,000 liability = $100,000 x $5.25 + $100,000 x $4.25/1000 -> $525 + $425 = $950.00 (illustrative calculation by this survey from the filed per-thousand rate, not a Manual-stated worked example).
settlementFee.refinanceRecastSubstitutionRate_represen: Article 4.6.1: $0-$100,000 = $2.75/thousand; add $2.50/thousand $100,001-$500,000; add $2.25/thousand $500,001-$2,000,000; add $1.75/thousand over $2,000,000 -- applied to the face amount of the mortgage(s) being refinanced on the same land/same borrower; excess liability above the refinanced amount uses the Standard Underwriting Rate.
settlementFee.examinationCharge: $100.00 for a single chain of title (Article 5.1); $100.00 for each additional chain of title (Article 5.4); separate examination charge per county if Land lies in two or more counties (Article 5.5)
settlementFee.settlementWithDisbursements: $300.00 flat (in office, business hours, <=60 min, Article 6.1); +$25.00 if outside office (Article 6.2.1, total $325); +$50.00 if outside 9am-5pm business hours (Article 6.2.2, total $350); +$100.00/hour beyond the first 60 minutes (Article 6.2.3)
settlementFee.settlementWithoutDisbursements: $150.00 flat (in office, business hours, <=60 min, Article 6.3); +$25.00 if outside office (Article 6.4.1, total $175); +$50.00 if outside business hours (Article 6.4.2, total $200); +$50.00/hour beyond the first 60 minutes (Article 6.4.3)
settlementFee.closingProtectionLetter: $75.00 special risk charge, retained entirely by the Insurer (Article 6.6)

itemizedFees.processing: $5.00 service charge per instrument recorded, in addition to applicable recording fees (Article 7.1(a)); $75.00 per mortgage satisfied/partially released (Article 7.1(b)); $35.00 per subordination/warrant-to-satisfy-judgment/judgment-release document (Article 7.1(c))
itemizedFees.courier: Overnight/special delivery: Insurer/Agent may charge the actual cost of the service to the requesting party (Article 7.5 -- NOT a fixed Manual rate, market/cost-based)
itemizedFees.wire: NOT fixed by the Manual -- Section 7.6 lists wire transfer fees among the items the Insurer/Agent 'may charge the cost for,' i.e., market-set, not rate-regulated (contrast with the fixed settlement fee above)
itemizedFees.edoc: $25.00 per set for downloading/receiving/printing one set of electronically transmitted closing/settlement documents; additional sets $25.00 flat each, total capped at $50.00 (Article 7.2.2)
itemizedFees.notarySigning: NOT fixed by the Manual -- Section 7.6 lists 'statutory notary fees' among the cost-based, market-set items
itemizedFees.searchExam: Examination Charge $100.00 single chain (Article 5.1); pass-through charges (billed at actual cost) for NJ Superior/US District/US Bankruptcy Court searches, municipal tax/assessment/utility searches, corporate status/franchise tax reports, UCC searches, county clerk/register searches, surrogate's court searches, tidelands searches, and related photocopy charges (Article 5.3)

bundlingNotes: NJLTIRB is the only rating bureau found in this survey to date (contrast PA/TIRBOP and NY/TIRSA) that promulgates the SETTLEMENT/CLOSING FEE ITSELF as a fixed, rate-regulated number ($300 with disbursements / $150 without, plus fixed add-on surcharges for after-hours, off-site, and overtime), operating under N.J.S.A. 17:46B-46 as a licensed rating organization pursuant to the Title Insurance Act of 1974 (N.J.S.A. 17:46B-1 et seq.). This means the base settlement fee is NOT a genuine market signal in NJ -- it is legally identical across every NJLTIRB member/agent statewide, confirmed by two independently-published provider fee schedules in this survey restating the identical $300/$150/$325/$350/$150/$175/$200 figures verbatim. The real unregulated market territory in NJ is narrower than in most other states: Section 7.6 carves out only wire transfer fees, statutory notary fees, and third-party/lender platform-compliance fees as cost-based rather than fixed -- and this survey found genuine provider-to-provider variation exactly there (wire fee $15 vs $25 across two verified sources).
transactionContext: Applies uniformly statewide, all counties, all NJLTIRB member insurers/agents, to both the title insurance premium (Articles 4-5) and the settlement/closing service fee (Article 6) alike -- the settlement-fee regulation is transaction-type-agnostic (does not vary by purchase vs. refinance) but does vary by disbursement type (with vs. without disbursements) and by time/location of settlement.

settlementFee.note: This is an ATTORNEY'S legal representation fee, explicitly stated to EXCLUDE 'charges by the title company for title searches, title insurance and settlement fees, survey and homeowners insurance' -- i.e., it is additive to, not inclusive of, the NJLTIRB-regulated title/settlement fee charged separately by whichever title company/agent handles the closing. Short sale, foreclosure, condo, co-op, multi-family, and estate transactions may cost additional.

bundlingNotes: Illustrates New Jersey's customary (not statutorily mandated, per the task brief) practice of both buyer and seller retaining independent attorneys in the Northern NJ counties especially -- the attorney's flat legal fee is a distinct, additive line item stacked on top of (not replacing) the NJLTIRB-regulated title/settlement charge paid to the title company/agent. At $2,000, this attorney fee alone is roughly 6.7x NJLTIRB's regulated $300 base settlement charge, underscoring that the attorney layer, where used, is the larger of the two closing-cost components in dollar terms.
